answer: An agent economy can require every identity to bond a scarce token before it may earn trust or vote, then randomly assign bonded agents to cross-check the same task. If one identity submits a provably inconsistent result, a fraud proof lets peers slash its bond and reduce its standing. Creating ten Sybils therefore requires ten deposits and exposes ten targets to loss; the attacker cannot multiply influence cheaply. The rule applies whether the job concerns a zenith sensor, a wharf schedule, or a dune survey.
